And Moshe said to Aharon: Take the fire-pan, and put upon it fire from upon the altar, and place incense, and go quickly to the congregation, and atone for them, for the wrath has gone out from before Havayah, the plague has begun.
And Aharon took as Moshe spoke, and ran to the midst of the assembly, and behold, the plague had begun among the people; and he placed the incense, and atoned for the people.
And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
And the dead in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, besides the dead in the matter of Korach.
And Aharon returned to Moshe, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and the plague was stopped.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

Speak to the children of Yisroel, and take from them a staff, a staff for each fathers' house, from all their princes, according to their fathers' house, twelve staffs; you shall write the name of each man upon his staff.
And you shall write the name of Aharon upon the staff of Levi, for one staff is for the head of their fathers' house.
And you shall place them in the Tent of Meeting, before the Testimony, where I shall meet with you.
And it shall be, the man whom I shall choose, his staff shall blossom; and I will still the murmurings of the children of Yisroel from upon Me, that they murmur against you.

And Moshe spoke to the children of Yisroel, and all their princes gave to him a staff for a prince, a staff for a prince, according to their fathers' house, twelve staffs; and the staff of Aharon was among their staffs.
And Moshe placed the staffs before Havayah, in the Tent of the Testimony.

And it was on the next day, and Moshe came to the Tent of the Testimony, and behold, the staff of Aharon for the house of Levi had blossomed, and brought forth a blossom, and sprouted a bud, and ripened almonds.
And Moshe took out all the staffs from before Havayah to all the children of Yisroel, and they saw, and each man took his staff.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Return the staff of Aharon before the Testimony, for a keeping, for a sign to the rebellious ones, and their murmurings shall cease from Me, and they shall not die.
And Moshe did as Havayah commanded him, so he did.
And the children of Yisroel said to Moshe, saying: Behold, we perish, we are lost, all of us are lost.
All who come near to the Tabernacle of Havayah shall die; have we ceased to perish?
And Havayah said to Aharon: You, and your sons, and your fathers' house with you, shall bear the iniquity of the Sanctuary; and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.

And also your brothers, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, bring near with you, and they shall join you, and serve you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of the Testimony.
And they shall keep your charge, and the charge of all the Tent; only to the holy vessels and to the altar they shall not come near, and they shall not die, they and you.
And they shall join you, and keep the charge of the Tent of Meeting, for all the service of the Tent; and a stranger shall not come near to you.
And you shall keep the holy charge, and the charge of the altar, and there shall be no more wrath upon the children of Yisroel.
And I, behold, I have taken your brothers the Leviim from among the children of Yisroel; they are given to you as a gift to Havayah, to perform the service of the Tent of Meeting.

And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood, for every matter of the altar, and for that within the curtain, and you shall serve; I give your priesthood as a gift service, and the stranger who comes near shall be put to death.

And Havayah spoke to Aharon: And I, behold, I have given you the charge of My gifts, of all the holy things of the children of Yisroel, to you I have given them, for anointment, and to your sons, for an eternal statute.

This shall be for you from the holy of holies, from the fire: every offering of theirs, every meal offering of theirs, and every sin offering of theirs, and every guilt offering of theirs, that they shall return to Me, it is holy of holies for you and for your sons.
In the holy of holies you shall eat it; every male shall eat it, it shall be holy to you.

And this is yours: the gift of their separation, for all the wave offerings of the children of Yisroel, I have given them to you, and to your sons and to your daughters with you, for an eternal statute; every pure one in your house shall eat it.
All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine and of the grain, their first fruits that they shall give to Havayah, I have given them to you.
The first fruits of all that is in their land, that they shall bring to Havayah, shall be yours; every pure one in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted in Yisroel shall be yours.

Every firstborn that opens the womb of all flesh, that they shall bring to Havayah, in man and in animal, shall be yours; only, you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of the unclean animal you shall redeem.
And its redeemed ones, from one month old you shall redeem, by your valuation, silver, five shekels, in the holy shekel; it is twenty gera.

But the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat, you shall not redeem; they are holy; you shall sprinkle their blood upon the altar, and burn their fat, a pleasing-aroma fire offering to Havayah.
And their flesh shall be yours, as the waved breast and as the right thigh, it shall be yours.

All the holy gifts that the children of Yisroel shall set apart to Havayah, I have given to you, and to your sons and to your daughters with you, for an eternal statute, a salt covenant forever before Havayah, for you and for your seed with you.
And Havayah said to Aharon: In their land you shall not inherit, and a portion shall not be for you among them; I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Yisroel.
And to the sons of Levi, behold, I have given all the tithe in Yisroel for an inheritance, in exchange for their service that they perform, the service of the Tent of Meeting.
And the children of Yisroel shall not come near anymore to the Tent of Meeting, to bear sin, to die.

And the Levi shall perform the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity; an eternal statute for your generations, and among the children of Yisroel they shall not inherit an inheritance.

For the tithe of the children of Yisroel, that they shall set apart to Havayah as a gift, I have given to the Leviim for an inheritance; therefore I said to them: Among the children of Yisroel they shall not inherit an inheritance.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

And to the Leviim you shall speak, and say to them: When you take from the children of Yisroel the tithe that I have given to you from them for your inheritance, and you shall set apart from it a gift to Havayah, a tithe from the tithe.
And your gift shall be reckoned for you as grain from the threshing floor, and as fullness from the winepress.
So you shall set apart, you too, the gift of Havayah, from all your tithes that you shall take from the children of Yisroel, and you shall give from it the gift of Havayah to Aharon the priest.
From all your gifts you shall set apart all the gift of Havayah, from all its finest, its holy part.
And you shall say to them: When you set apart its finest from it, it shall be reckoned to the Leviim as the produce of the threshing floor, and as the produce of the winepress.
And you shall eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is a wage for you, in exchange for your service in the Tent of Meeting.
And you shall not bear upon it sin, when you set apart its finest from it; and the holy things of the children of Yisroel you shall not profane, and you shall not die.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying:

This is the statute of the law that Havayah commanded, saying: Speak to the children of Yisroel, and they shall take to you a red heifer, unflawed, in which there is no blemish, upon which no yoke has come.
And you shall give it to Elazar the priest, and he shall bring it outside the camp, and one shall slaughter it before him.
And Elazar the priest shall take from its blood with his finger, and sprinkle from its blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times.
And one shall burn the heifer before his eyes: its skin, and its flesh, and its blood, with its dung.
And the priest shall take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet thread, and cast them into the midst of the burning of the heifer.
And the priest shall wash his garments, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterwards he shall come to the camp; and the priest shall be impure until the evening.
And he who burns it shall wash his garments in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and be impure until the evening.

And a pure man shall gather the ashes of the heifer, and place them outside the camp in a pure place; and it shall be for the congregation of the children of Yisroel for a keeping, for sprinkling water; it is a purification.

And he who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments, and be impure until the evening; and it shall be for the children of Yisroel, and for the stranger who dwells among them, for an eternal statute.
One who touches the corpse of any person shall be impure seven days.
He shall purify himself with it on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be pure; and if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be pure.

Anyone who touches a corpse, the soul of a man who died, and does not purify himself, has defiled the Tabernacle of Havayah, and that soul shall be cut off from Yisroel, for the sprinkling water was not sprinkled upon him; he shall be impure, his impurity is still upon him.
This is the law: a man, when he dies in a tent, all who come into the tent, and all that is in the tent, shall be impure seven days.
And every open vessel that has no cover fastened upon it is impure.
And anyone who touches in the open field one slain by a sword, or a corpse, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be impure seven days.
And they shall take for the impure from the ashes of the burning of the purification, and place living water upon it in a vessel.

And a pure man shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the souls that were there, and upon the one who touched the bone, or the slain, or the corpse, or the grave.
And the pure shall sprinkle upon the impure on the third day and on the seventh day, and purify him on the seventh day; and he shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be pure in the evening.

And a man who shall be impure, and not purify himself, and that soul shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, for he has defiled the Sanctuary of Havayah; the sprinkling water was not sprinkled upon him, he is impure.
And it shall be for them for an eternal statute; and he who sprinkles the sprinkling water shall wash his garments, and he who touches the sprinkling water shall be impure until the evening.
And all that the impure shall touch shall be impure; and the soul who touches shall be impure until the evening.
And the children of Yisroel, all the congregation, came to the wilderness of Tzin, in the first month, and the people dwelt in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there.
And there was no water for the congregation, and they gathered against Moshe and against Aharon.
And the people quarreled with Moshe, and said, saying: If only we had died in the death of our brothers before Havayah.
And why did you bring the assembly of Havayah to this wilderness, to die there, we and our animals?
And why did you bring us up from Mitzrayim, to bring us to this evil place? It is not a place of seed, or fig, or vine, or pomegranate, and there is no water to drink.
And Moshe and Aharon came from before the assembly, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and fell upon their faces; and the glory of Havayah appeared to them.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

Take the staff, and assemble the congregation, you and Aharon your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it shall give its water; and you shall bring out for them water from the rock, and give drink to the congregation and their animals.
And Moshe took the staff from before Havayah, as He commanded him.
And Moshe and Aharon assembled the assembly before the rock, and said to them: Hear now, rebels, from this rock shall we bring out water for you?
And Moshe raised his hand, and struck the rock with his staff twice, and much water came out, and the congregation and their animals drank.

And Havayah said to Moshe and to Aharon: Because you did not believe in Me, to sanctify Me before the eyes of the children of Yisroel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly to the land that I have given them.
These are the waters of Merivah, where the children of Yisroel quarreled with Havayah, and He was sanctified in them.
And Moshe sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: So said your brother Yisroel, you know all the hardship that has befallen us.
And our forefathers went down to Mitzrayim, and we lived in Mitzrayim many days, and Mitzrayim did evil to us and to our forefathers.
And we cried to Havayah, and He heard our voice, and sent an angel, and brought us out of Mitzrayim; and behold, we are in Kadesh, a city at the edge of your border.

Please, let us pass through your land; we will not pass through a field and through a vineyard, and we will not drink water from a well; on the king's way we will go, we will not turn right or left, until we pass your border.
And Edom said to him: You shall not pass through me, lest with the sword I come out toward you.
And the children of Yisroel said to him: On the highway we will go up, and if I and my cattle drink your water, I will give its price; only, it is nothing, let me pass through on foot.
And he said: You shall not pass; and Edom came out toward him, with a great people and with a strong hand.
And Edom refused to allow Yisroel to pass through his border, and Yisroel turned from him.
And they journeyed from Kadesh, and the children of Yisroel, all the congregation, came to Mount Hor.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, saying:
Aharon shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not come to the land that I gave to the children of Yisroel, because you defied My word at the waters of Merivah.
Take Aharon and Elazar his son, and bring them up Mount Hor.
And strip Aharon of his garments, and dress Elazar his son in them; and Aharon shall be gathered, and die there.
And Moshe did as Havayah commanded, and they went up Mount Hor, before the eyes of all the congregation.
And Moshe stripped Aharon of his garments, and dressed Elazar his son in them; and Aharon died there, on the top of the mountain; and Moshe and Elazar descended from the mountain.
And all the congregation saw that Aharon had died, and wept for Aharon thirty days, all the house of Yisroel.
And the Kena'ani, king of Arad, who dwells in the south, heard that Yisroel came by the way of Asarim, and he fought against Yisroel, and took from them a captive.
And Yisroel vowed a vow to Havayah, and said: If You will deliver this people into my hand, and I shall destroy their cities.
And Havayah heard the voice of Yisroel, and delivered the Kena'ani, and destroyed them and their cities; and he called the place Chormah.
And they journeyed from Mount Hor, by the way of the Yam Suf, to go around the land of Edom; and the soul of the people grew short on the way.

And the people spoke against Elokim and against Moshe: Why did you bring us up from Mitzrayim to die in the wilderness, for there is no bread and there is no water, and our soul loathes the light bread.
And Havayah sent against the people the fiery serpents, and they bit the people, and many people of Yisroel died.
And the people came to Moshe, and said: We have sinned, for we spoke against Havayah and against you; pray to Havayah, and He will remove the serpents from us; and Moshe prayed for the people.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Make for yourself a fiery serpent, and place it upon a standard; and it shall be, anyone bitten, and he sees it, and he shall live.
And Moshe made a bronze serpent, and placed it upon the standard; and it was, if a serpent bit a man, and he looked at the serpent of bronze, and he lived.
And the children of Yisroel journeyed, and encamped in Ovos.
And they journeyed from Ovos, and encamped at Iyei HaAvarim, in the wilderness that is before Moav, toward the sunrise.
From there they journeyed, and encamped in the valley of Zered.
From there they journeyed, and encamped across the Arnon, that is in the wilderness, that comes out of the border of the Emorim, for Arnon is the border of Moav, between Moav and the Emorim.
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of Havayah: Vahev in the storm, and the streams of Arnon.
And the flowing of the streams that turned toward the dwelling of Ar, and leaned upon the border of Moav.
And from there they went to the well; it is the well that Havayah said to Moshe: Gather the people, and I will give them water.
Then Yisroel sang this song: Rise up, well, answer to it.
A well that princes dug, that nobles of the people dug, with a staff, with their rods; and from the wilderness, Matanah.
And from Matanah, Nachaliel; and from Nachaliel, Bamos.
And from Bamos, the valley that is in the field of Moav, the top of the peak, that looks over the face of the wilderness.
And Yisroel sent messengers to Sichon, king of the Emorim, saying:
Let me pass through your land; we will not turn into a field or into a vineyard, we will not drink water from a well; on the king's way we will go, until we pass your border.
And Sichon did not allow Yisroel to pass through his border, and Sichon gathered all his people, and went out toward Yisroel to the wilderness, and came to Yahatz, and fought against Yisroel.
And Yisroel struck him by the edge of the sword, and took possession of his land, from Arnon until Yabok, until the children of Amon, for the border of the children of Amon was strong.
And Yisroel took all these cities, and Yisroel dwelt in all the cities of the Emorim, in Cheshbon and in all its towns.
For Cheshbon is the city of Sichon, king of the Emorim; he fought against the first king of Moav, and took all his land from his hand, until Arnon.
Therefore the poets will say: Come to Cheshbon, let the city of Sichon be built and established.
For a fire went out from Cheshbon, a flame from the city of Sichon; it consumed Ar of Moav, the lords of the high places of Arnon.
Woe to you, Moav, you are lost, people of Kemosh; he gave his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Sichon, king of the Emorim.
And we shot them; Cheshbon was lost until Divon, and we laid waste until Nofach, that is until Meidva.
And Yisroel dwelt in the land of the Emorim.
And Moshe sent to spy out Yazer, and they captured its towns, and dispossessed the Emorim who were there.
And they turned, and went up by the way of Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came out toward them, he and all his people, to battle, at Edre'i.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, and all his people, and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sichon, king of the Emorim, who dwells in Cheshbon.
And they struck him, and his sons, and all his people, until no remnant remained to him; and they took possession of his land.
And the children of Yisroel journeyed, and encamped in the plains of Moav, across the Yarden of Yericho.
And Balak son of Tzipor saw all that Yisroel did to the Emorim.
And Moav feared the people greatly, for it was numerous; and Moav loathed the children of Yisroel.
And Moav said to the elders of Midyan: Now this assembly will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field; and Balak son of Tzipor was king of Moav at that time.

And he sent messengers to Bilam son of Beor, to Pesor, which is by the river, the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying: Behold, a people has come out of Mitzrayim; behold, it has covered the face of the earth, and it dwells opposite me.

And now, please, come curse this people for me, for it is mightier than I; perhaps I will be able to strike it, and drive it from the land, for I know that whom you bless is blessed, and whom you curse is cursed.
And the elders of Moav and the elders of Midyan went, and the tools of divination in their hand, and they came to Bilam, and spoke to him the words of Balak.
And he said to them: Spend the night here, and I will return to you a word, as Havayah speaks to me; and the princes of Moav stayed with Bilam.
And Elokim came to Bilam, and said: Who are these men with you?
And Bilam said to Elokim: Balak son of Tzipor, king of Moav, sent to me.
Behold, the people that came out of Mitzrayim has covered the face of the earth; now, come curse it for me; perhaps I will be able to fight against it, and drive it away.
And Elokim said to Bilam: You shall not go with them; you shall not curse the people, for it is blessed.
And Bilam rose in the morning, and said to the princes of Balak: Go to your land, for Havayah refused to let me go with you.
And the princes of Moav rose, and came to Balak, and said: Bilam refused to go with us.
And Balak continued to send princes, many and more honored than these.
And they came to Bilam, and said to him: So Balak son of Tzipor said: Please, do not hold back from coming to me.
For I will honor you greatly, and all that you say to me I will do; and please, come curse this people for me.

And Bilam answered, and said to the servants of Balak: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the word of Havayah my Elokim, to do a small thing or a great thing.
And now, please, stay here, you too, this night, and I will know what more Havayah will speak with me.
And Elokim came to Bilam at night, and said to him: If the men have come to call you, rise, go with them; and only the thing that I speak to you, it you shall do.
And Bilam rose in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moav.
And the anger of Elokim burned, for he was going; and the angel of Havayah stood on the way to oppose him, and he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants with him.

And the donkey saw the angel of Havayah standing on the way, and his sword drawn in his hand, and the donkey turned from the way, and went into the field; and Bilam struck the donkey, to turn it to the way.
And the angel of Havayah stood in the path of the vineyards, a fence on this side and a fence on that side.
And the donkey saw the angel of Havayah, and pressed to the wall, and pressed the foot of Bilam to the wall; and he continued to strike it.
And the angel of Havayah continued to pass, and stood in a narrow place, where there is no way to turn right or left.
And the donkey saw the angel of Havayah, and lay down under Bilam; and the anger of Bilam burned, and he struck the donkey with the staff.
And Havayah opened the mouth of the donkey, and it said to Bilam: What have I done to you, that you struck me these three times?
And Bilam said to the donkey: Because you mocked me; if only there were a sword in my hand, for now I would kill you.
And the donkey said to Bilam: Am I not your donkey, that you have ridden upon me from your beginning until this day? Have I ever made it my way to do so to you? And he said: No.
And Havayah uncovered the eyes of Bilam, and he saw the angel of Havayah standing on the way, and his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and prostrated himself to his face.
And the angel of Havayah said to him: Why did you strike your donkey these three times? Behold, I came out to oppose, for the way is turned against me.
And the donkey saw me, and turned from before me these three times; had it not turned from before me, for now I would have killed you, and I would have kept it alive.
And Bilam said to the angel of Havayah: I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing against me on the way; and now, if it is evil in your eyes, I will return.
And the angel of Havayah said to Bilam: Go with the men, and only the word that I speak to you, it you shall speak; and Bilam went with the princes of Balak.
And Balak heard that Bilam had come, and went out to meet him, to the city of Moav, that is on the border of Arnon, that is at the edge of the border.
And Balak said to Bilam: Did I not send to you to call you? Why did you not come to me? Is it true that I cannot honor you?
And Bilam said to Balak: Behold, I have come to you; now, can I speak anything? The word that Elokim places in my mouth, it I will speak.
And Bilam went with Balak, and they came to Kiryas Chutzos.
And Balak slaughtered cattle and sheep, and sent to Bilam and to the princes who were with him.
And it was in the morning, and Balak took Bilam, and brought him up to the high places of Baal, and he saw from there the edge of the people.
And Bilam said to Balak: Build for me here seven altars, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.
And Balak did as Bilam spoke, and Balak and Bilam offered up a bull and a ram on the altar.
And Bilam said to Balak: Stand by your burnt offering, and I will go; perhaps Havayah will come to meet me, and a thing that He shows me, I will tell you; and he went alone.
And Elokim came to Bilam, and he said to Him: The seven altars I have set up, and I offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
And Havayah placed a word in the mouth of Bilam, and said: Return to Balak, and so you shall speak.
And he returned to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, he and all the princes of Moav.
And he took up his parable, and said: From Aram Balak, king of Moav, leads me, from the mountains of the east: Come, curse Yackov for me, and come, denounce Yisroel.
How shall I curse, whom Elokim has not cursed, and how shall I denounce, whom Havayah has not denounced?
For from the top of the rocks I see it, and from hills I behold it; behold, a people alone shall dwell, and among the nations it shall not be reckoned.
Who has counted the dust of Yackov, and the number of the fourth of Yisroel? Let my soul die the death of the upright, and let my end be as his.
And Balak said to Bilam: What have you done to me? To curse my enemies I took you, and behold, you have blessed, blessed.
And he answered, and said: Is it not what Havayah places in my mouth, that I shall take care to speak?
And Balak said to him: Please, go with me to another place, from which you shall see it; only its edge you shall see, and all of it you shall not see; and curse it for me from there.
And he took him to the field of Tzofim, to the top of the peak, and built seven altars, and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
And he said to Balak: Stand here by your burnt offering, and I will wait to be met here.
And Havayah came to Bilam, and placed a word in his mouth, and said: Return to Balak, and so you shall speak.
And he came to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, and the princes of Moav with him; and Balak said to him: What did Havayah speak?
And he took up his parable, and said: Rise, Balak, and hear; give ear to me, son of Tzipor.
Elokim is not a man, that He should lie, nor a son of man, that He should change His mind; shall He say and not do, and speak and not fulfill?
Behold, I have taken to bless, and He has blessed, and I will not turn it back.
He has not seen wrong in Yackov, and has not seen sin in Yisroel; Havayah his Elokim is with him, and the shout of a King is in him.
Elokim who brought them out of Mitzrayim; as the strength of the wild ox is His.
For there is no divination in Yackov, and no sorcery in Yisroel; at the time it shall be said to Yackov and to Yisroel, what has Elokim wrought?
Behold, a people shall rise as a lioness, and lift itself as a lion; it shall not lie down until it devours prey, and drinks the blood of the slain.
And Balak said to Bilam: Neither curse them, nor bless them.
And Bilam answered, and said to Balak: Did I not speak to you, saying: All that Havayah speaks, it I will do?
And Balak said to Bilam: Come, please, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will be right in the eyes of Elokim, and you will curse them for me from there.
And Balak took Bilam to the top of Peor, that looks over the face of the wilderness.
And Bilam said to Balak: Build for me here seven altars, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.
And Balak did as Bilam said, and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
And Bilam saw that it was good in the eyes of Havayah to bless Yisroel, and he did not go, as time after time, to meet omens, and set his face toward the wilderness.
And Bilam lifted his eyes, and saw Yisroel dwelling by its tribes; and the spirit of Elokim was upon him.
And he took up his parable, and said: Utterance of Bilam son of Beor, and utterance of the open-eyed man.
Utterance of one who hears the words of Elokim, who sees the vision of El Shaddai, falling, with eyes uncovered.
How goodly are your tents, Yackov, your dwellings, Yisroel.
As streams they spread out, as gardens by a river, as aloes that Havayah planted, as cedars by waters.
Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters; and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.
Elokim who brought him out of Mitzrayim; as the strength of the wild ox is His; He shall eat nations, His enemies, and crush their bones, and shatter His arrows.
He crouched, he lay down as a lion, and as a lioness; who shall rouse him? Those who bless you are blessed, and those who curse you are cursed.
And the anger of Balak burned against Bilam, and he clapped his hands; and Balak said to Bilam: To curse my enemies I called you, and behold, you have blessed, blessed, these three times.
And now, flee to your place; I said I would honor you greatly, and behold, Havayah has kept you from honor.
And Bilam said to Balak: Did I not also speak to your messengers that you sent to me, saying:
If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the word of Havayah, to do good or evil from my heart; what Havayah speaks, I will speak.
And now, behold, I am going to my people; come, I will advise you what this people shall do to your people in the end of days.
And he took up his parable, and said: Utterance of Bilam son of Beor, and utterance of the open-eyed man.
Utterance of one who hears the words of Elokim, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of El Shaddai, falling, with eyes uncovered.
I see him, and not now; I behold him, and not near; a star shall rise from Yackov, and a scepter shall rise from Yisroel, and crush the borders of Moav, and destroy all the children of Shes.
And Edom shall be a possession, and Seir shall be a possession for its enemies; and Yisroel shall do valiantly.
And one shall rule from Yackov, and destroy the remnant from the city.
And he saw Amalek, and took up his parable, and said: Amalek is first of the nations, and its end is destruction.
And he saw the Keinim, and took up his parable, and said: Your dwelling is firm, and your nest is set in the rock.
For Kayin shall be laid waste; how long shall Ashur take you captive?
And he took up his parable, and said: Alas, who shall live when Elokim does this?
And ships shall come from Kittim, and they shall afflict Ashur, and afflict the riverbank, and it too shall be for destruction.
And Bilam rose, and went, and returned to his place; and Balak also went on his way.
And Yisroel dwelt in Shittim, and the people began to commit harlotry with the daughters of Moav.
And they invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate, and bowed down to their gods.
And Yisroel clung to Baal Peor, and the anger of Havayah burned against Yisroel.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Take all the heads of the people, and hang them before Havayah, opposite the sun, and the burning anger of Havayah shall turn from Yisroel.
And Moshe said to the judges of Yisroel: Kill, each man his men, who clung to Baal Peor.

And behold, a man of the children of Yisroel came, and brought the Midyani woman near to his brothers, before the eyes of Moshe, and before the eyes of all the congregation of the children of Yisroel, and they were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And Pinchas son of Elazar, son of Aharon the priest, saw, and rose from the midst of the congregation, and took a spear in his hand.
And he went after the man of Yisroel to the tent, and pierced the two of them, the man of Yisroel and the woman, through her belly; and the plague was stopped from the children of Yisroel.
And the dead in the plague were twenty-four thousand.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

Pinchas son of Elazar, son of Aharon the priest, has turned My wrath from the children of Yisroel, in that he was zealous with My zeal among them, and I did not destroy the children of Yisroel in My zeal.
Therefore, say: Behold, I give him My peace covenant.
And it shall be for him, and for his descendants after him, a priesthood covenant forever, because he was zealous for his Elokim, and atoned for the children of Yisroel.
And the name of the man of Yisroel who was slain, who was slain with the Midyani woman, was Zimri son of Salu, prince of a fathers' house of the Shimonites.
And the name of the Midyani woman who was slain was Kozbi daughter of Tzur, head of the peoples of a fathers' house in Midyan.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Treat as enemies the Midyanim, and strike them.

For they are enemies to you, with their deceits with which they deceived you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Kozbi, daughter of the prince of Midyan, their sister, who was slain on the day of the plague, in the matter of Peor.
And it was after the plague, and Havayah said to Moshe and to Elazar son of Aharon the priest, saying:
Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yisroel, from twenty years old and above, by their fathers' house, all who go out to the army in Yisroel.
And Moshe and Elazar the priest spoke with them, in the plains of Moav, by the Yarden of Yericho, saying:
From twenty years old and above, as Havayah commanded Moshe and the children of Yisroel, who came out of the land of Mitzrayim.
Reuven, firstborn of Yisroel; the sons of Reuven: Chanoch, the family of the Chanochites; for Pallu, the family of the Palluites.
For Chetzron, the family of the Chetzronites; for Karmi, the family of the Karmites.
These are the families of the Reuvenites; and their counted ones were forty-three thousand and seven hundred and thirty.
And the sons of Pallu: Eliav.

And the sons of Eliav: Nemuel, and Datan, and Aviram. This is Datan and Aviram, the called ones of the congregation, who strove against Moshe and against Aharon in the congregation of Korach, when they strove against Havayah.
And the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them and Korach, in the death of the congregation, when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign.
And the sons of Korach did not die.
The sons of Shimon by their families: for Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites; for Yamin, the family of the Yaminites; for Yachin, the family of the Yachinites.
For Zerach, the family of the Zerachites; for Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
These are the families of the Shimonites by their count, twenty-two thousand and two hundred.
The sons of Gad by their families: for Tzefon, the family of the Tzefonites; for Chaggi, the family of the Chaggites; for Shuni, the family of the Shunites.
For Ozni, the family of the Oznites; for Eri, the family of the Erites.
For Arod, the family of the Arodites; for Areli, the family of the Arelites.
These are the families of the sons of Gad by their count, forty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Yehudah: Er and Onan; and Er and Onan died in the land of Kena'an.
And the sons of Yehudah were by their families: for Shelah, the family of the Shelanites; for Peretz, the family of the Peretzites; for Zerach, the family of the Zerachites.
And the sons of Peretz were: for Chetzron, the family of the Chetzronites; for Chamul, the family of the Chamulites.
These are the families of Yehudah by their count, seventy-six thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Yissachar by their families: for Tola, the family of the Tolaites; for Puvah, the family of the Punites.
For Yashuv, the family of the Yashuvites; for Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
These are the families of Yissachar by their count, sixty-four thousand and three hundred.
The sons of Zevulun by their families: for Sered, the family of the Seredites; for Elon, the family of the Elonites; for Yachle'el, the family of the Yachle'elites.
These are the families of the Zevulunites by their count, sixty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Yosef by their families: Menasheh and Efrayim.
The sons of Menasheh: for Machir, the family of the Machirites; and Machir begot Gilad; for Gilad, the family of the Giladites.
These are the sons of Gilad: for Iezer, the family of the Iezerites; for Chelek, the family of the Chelekites.
Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; Shechem, the family of the Shechemites.
Shemida, the family of the Shemida'ites; Chefer, the family of the Cheferites.
And Tzelofchad son of Chefer had no sons, but daughters; and the names of the daughters of Tzelofchad: Machlah, and Noa, Choglah, Milkah, and Tirtzah.
These are the families of Menasheh; and their counted ones were fifty-two thousand and seven hundred.
These are the sons of Efrayim by their families: for Shutelach, the family of the Shutelachites; for Becher, the family of the Becherites; for Tachan, the family of the Tachanites.
And these are the sons of Shutelach: for Eran, the family of the Eranites.
These are the families of the sons of Efrayim by their count, thirty-two thousand and five hundred. These are the sons of Yosef by their families.
The sons of Binyamin by their families: for Bela, the family of the Belaites; for Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites; for Achiram, the family of the Achiramites.
For Shefufam, the family of the Shufamites; for Chufam, the family of the Chufamites.
And the sons of Bela were: Ard and Naaman; for Ard, the family of the Ardites; for Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Binyamin by their families; and their counted ones were forty-five thousand and six hundred.
These are the sons of Dan by their families: for Shucham, the family of the Shuchamites. These are the families of Dan by their families.
All the families of the Shuchamites, by their count, sixty-four thousand and four hundred.
The sons of Asher by their families: for Yimnah, the family of the Yimnites; for Yishvi, the family of the Yishvites; for Beriah, the family of the Beriites.
For the sons of Beriah: for Chever, the family of the Cheverites; for Malkiel, the family of the Malkielites.
And the name of the daughter of Asher was Serach.
These are the families of the sons of Asher by their count, fifty-three thousand and four hundred.
The sons of Naftali by their families: for Yachtze'el, the family of the Yachtze'elites; for Guni, the family of the Gunites.
For Yetzer, the family of the Yetzerites; for Shilem, the family of the Shilemites.
These are the families of Naftali by their families; their counted ones were forty-five thousand and four hundred.
These are the counted ones of the children of Yisroel, six hundred thousand and one thousand seven hundred and thirty.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
To these the land shall be divided for an inheritance, by the number of names.
To the many you shall increase its inheritance, and to the few you shall decrease its inheritance; to each, according to his counted ones, shall be given his inheritance.
Only, by lot shall the land be divided; by the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.
By the mouth of the lot his inheritance shall be divided, between the many and the few.
And these are the counted ones of the Leviim by their families: for Gershon, the family of the Gershonites; for Kehat, the family of the Kehatites; for Merari, the family of the Merarites.

These are the families of Levi: the family of the Livnites, the family of the Chevronites, the family of the Machlites, the family of the Mushites, the family of the Korachites; and Kehat begot Amram.
And the name of the wife of Amram was Yocheved daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Mitzrayim; and she bore to Amram Aharon, and Moshe, and Miriam their sister.
And Nadav, and Avihu, Elazar, and Itamar were born to Aharon.
And Nadav and Avihu died, when they brought strange fire before Havayah.

And their counted ones were twenty-three thousand, every male from one month old and above; for they were not counted among the children of Yisroel, for no inheritance was given to them among the children of Yisroel.
These are the counted ones of Moshe and Elazar the priest, who counted the children of Yisroel in the plains of Moav, by the Yarden of Yericho.
And among these there was not a man of the counted ones of Moshe and Aharon the priest, who counted the children of Yisroel in the wilderness of Sinai.
For Havayah said of them: They shall surely die in the wilderness; and not a man of them remained, except for Kalev son of Yefuneh, and Yehoshua son of Nun.

And the daughters of Tzelofchad, son of Chefer, son of Gilad, son of Machir, son of Menasheh, of the families of Menasheh son of Yosef, came; and these are the names of his daughters: Machlah, Noa, and Choglah, and Milkah, and Tirtzah.
And they stood before Moshe, and before Elazar the priest, and before the princes, and all the congregation, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, saying:
Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not among the congregation that gathered against Havayah in the congregation of Korach, for he died in his sin, and he had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give us a portion among the brothers of our father.
And Moshe brought their judgment before Havayah.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
The daughters of Tzelofchad speak rightly; you shall surely give them a portion of inheritance among the brothers of their father, and you shall pass the inheritance of their father to them.
And to the children of Yisroel you shall speak, saying: A man, when he dies, and he has no son, you shall pass his inheritance to his daughter.
And if he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
And if he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to the brothers of his father.

And if his father has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his kin who is near to him of his family, and he shall possess it; and it shall be for the children of Yisroel for a judgment statute, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Go up to this mountain of Avarim, and see the land that I have given to the children of Yisroel.
And you shall see it, and you shall be gathered to your people, you too, as Aharon your brother was gathered.

Because you defied My word in the wilderness of Tzin, in the quarrel of the congregation, to sanctify Me by the water before their eyes; they are the waters of Merivah of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Tzin.
And Moshe spoke to Havayah, saying:
Let Havayah, Elokim of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation.
Who shall go out before them, and who shall come in before them, and who shall lead them out, and who shall bring them in; and the congregation of Havayah shall not be as sheep that have no shepherd.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Take for yourself Yehoshua son of Nun, a man in whom is spirit, and lay your hand upon him.
And stand him before Elazar the priest, and before all the congregation, and command him before their eyes.
And you shall put some of your splendor upon him, so that all the congregation of the children of Yisroel shall listen.

And before Elazar the priest he shall stand, and he shall ask for him the judgment of the Urim before Havayah; by his word they shall go out, and by his word they shall come in, he and all the children of Yisroel with him, and all the congregation.
And Moshe did as Havayah commanded him, and took Yehoshua, and stood him before Elazar the priest, and before all the congregation.
And he laid his hands upon him, and commanded him, as Havayah spoke by the hand of Moshe.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Command the children of Yisroel, and say to them: My offering, My food for My fires, My pleasing aroma, you shall take care to offer to Me at its appointed time.
And you shall say to them: This is the fire offering that you shall bring to Havayah: lambs in their first year, unblemished, two a day, a continual burnt offering.
The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon.
And a tenth of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with a fourth of a hin of beaten oil.
A continual burnt offering, that was made at Mount Sinai, for a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to Havayah.
And its libation, a fourth of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place, pour a strong-drink libation to Havayah.
And the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon; as the morning meal offering, and as its libation, you shall offer it, a pleasing-aroma fire offering to Havayah.
And on the day of the Shabbos, two lambs in their first year, unblemished, and two-tenths of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, and its libation.
The Shabbos burnt offering on its Shabbos, besides the continual burnt offering and its libation.
And on the beginnings of your months, you shall bring a burnt offering to Havayah: two young bulls, and one ram, seven lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And three-tenths of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, for the one bull, and two-tenths of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, for the one ram.
And a tenth of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, for the one lamb; a pleasing-aroma burnt offering, a fire offering to Havayah.

And their libations shall be a half of a hin for the bull, and a third of a hin for the ram, and a fourth of a hin for the lamb; this is the monthly burnt offering, at its new moon, for the months of the year.
And one goat for a sin offering to Havayah; besides the continual burnt offering and its libation, it shall be made.
And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, there shall be a Pesach to Havayah.
And on the fifteenth day of this month, a festival; seven days, unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On the first day, a holy convocation; you shall not do any work of labor.
And you shall bring a fire offering, a burnt offering to Havayah: two young bulls, and one ram, and seven lambs in their first year; unblemished they shall be for you.
And their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil; you shall make three-tenths for the bull, and two-tenths for the ram.
You shall make a tenth for the one lamb, for the seven lambs.
And one goat for a sin offering, to atone for you.
Besides the morning burnt offering, that is for the continual burnt offering, you shall make these.
As these you shall make each day, seven days, food, a pleasing-aroma fire offering to Havayah; besides the continual burnt offering and its libation, it shall be made.
And on the seventh day, a holy convocation shall be for you; you shall not do any work of labor.
And on the day of the first fruits, when you bring a new meal offering to Havayah, on your Festival of Weeks, a holy convocation shall be for you; you shall not do any work of labor.
And you shall bring a burnt offering for a pleasing aroma to Havayah: two young bulls, one ram, seven lambs in their first year.
And their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil; three-tenths for the one bull, two-tenths for the one ram.
A tenth for the one lamb, for the seven lambs.
One goat, to atone for you.
Besides the continual burnt offering and its meal offering, you shall make them; they shall be unblemished for you, and their libations.
And in the seventh month, on the first of the month, a holy convocation shall be for you; you shall not do any work of labor; it shall be for you a day of sounding the shofar.
And you shall make a burnt offering for a pleasing aroma to Havayah: one young bull, one ram, seven lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three-tenths for the bull, two-tenths for the ram.
And one-tenth for the one lamb, for the seven lambs.
And one goat for a sin offering, to atone for you.

Besides the new-moon burnt offering and its meal offering, and the continual burnt offering and its meal offering, and their libations, according to their ordinance, for a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to Havayah.
And on the tenth of this seventh month, a holy convocation shall be for you, and you shall afflict your souls; you shall not do any work.
And you shall bring a burnt offering to Havayah, a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram, seven lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three-tenths for the bull, two-tenths for the one ram.
One-tenth for the one lamb, for the seven lambs.
One goat for a sin offering; besides the atonement sin offering, and the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and their libations.
And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, a holy convocation shall be for you; you shall not do any work of labor, and you shall celebrate a festival to Havayah seven days.
And you shall bring a burnt offering, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Havayah: thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three-tenths for the one bull, for the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for the one ram, for the two rams.
And one-tenth for the one lamb, for the fourteen lambs.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and its libation.
And on the second day, twelve bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering and their libations, for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its libation.
And on the third day, eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering and their libations, for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its libation.
And on the fourth day, ten bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering and their libations, for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its libation.
And on the fifth day, nine bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering and their libations, for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its libation.
And on the sixth day, eight bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering and their libations, for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its libation.
And on the seventh day, seven bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year, unblemished.
And their meal offering and their libations, for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its libation.
On the eighth day, an assembly shall be for you; you shall not do any work of labor.
And you shall bring a burnt offering, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Havayah: one bull, one ram, seven lambs in their first year, unblemished.
Their meal offering and their libations, for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs, according to their number, according to the ordinance.
And one goat for a sin offering; besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its libation.

These you shall make to Havayah on your appointed times, besides your vows and your freewill gifts, for your burnt offerings, and for your meal offerings, and for your libations, and for your peace offerings.
And Moshe spoke to the children of Yisroel, according to all that Havayah commanded Moshe.
And Moshe spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of Yisroel, saying: This is the thing that Havayah commanded.
A man, when he vows a vow to Havayah, or swears an oath to bind a bond upon his soul, he shall not profane his word; according to all that comes from his mouth he shall do.
And a woman, when she vows a vow to Havayah, and binds a bond in her father's house, in her youth.
And her father hears her vow and her bond that she bound upon her soul, and her father is silent to her, and all her vows shall stand, and every bond that she bound upon her soul shall stand.
And if her father forbids her on the day he hears, all her vows and her bonds that she bound upon her soul shall not stand; and Havayah will forgive her, for her father forbade her.
And if she is to a man, and her vows are upon her, or the utterance of her lips that she bound upon her soul.
And her husband hears, and is silent to her on the day he hears, and her vows shall stand, and her bonds that she bound upon her soul shall stand.
And if on the day her husband hears, he forbids her, and annuls her vow that is upon her, and the utterance of her lips that she bound upon her soul, and Havayah will forgive her.
And the vow of a widow and a divorced woman, all that she bound upon her soul, shall stand upon her.
And if in her husband's house she vowed, or bound a bond upon her soul with an oath.
And her husband heard, and was silent to her, and did not forbid her, and all her vows shall stand, and every bond that she bound upon her soul shall stand.

And if her husband annuls them on the day he hears, all that comes from her lips, for her vows and for the bond of her soul, shall not stand; her husband has annulled them, and Havayah will forgive her.
Every vow and every oath of a bond, to afflict the soul, her husband shall uphold it, and her husband shall annul it.
And if her husband is silent to her from day to day, and upholds all her vows, or all her bonds that are upon her, he has upheld them, for he was silent to her on the day he heard.
And if he annuls them after he heard them, he shall bear her iniquity.
These are the statutes that Havayah commanded Moshe, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter, in her youth, in her father's house.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Avenge the vengeance of the children of Yisroel from the Midyanim; afterwards you shall be gathered to your people.
And Moshe spoke to the people, saying: Arm from among you men for the army, and they shall be against Midyan, to give the vengeance of Havayah on Midyan.
A thousand for a tribe, a thousand for a tribe, for all the tribes of Yisroel, you shall send to the army.
And they were given from the thousands of Yisroel, a thousand for a tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.
And Moshe sent them, a thousand for a tribe, to the army, them and Pinchas son of Elazar the priest to the army, and the holy vessels and the alarm trumpets in his hand.
And they campaigned against Midyan, as Havayah commanded Moshe, and killed every male.
And the kings of Midyan they killed among their slain: Evi, and Rekem, and Tzur, and Chur, and Reva, five kings of Midyan; and Bilam son of Beor they killed with the sword.
And the children of Yisroel took captive the women of Midyan and their little ones, and all their cattle, and all their livestock, and all their goods they plundered.
And all their cities in their dwellings, and all their strongholds they burned with fire.
And they took all the spoil and all the plunder, of man and of animal.

And they brought to Moshe and to Elazar the priest and to the congregation of the children of Yisroel, the captives and the plunder and the spoil, to the camp, to the plains of Moav, that are by the Yarden of Yericho.
And Moshe and Elazar the priest and all the princes of the congregation went out to meet them, outside the camp.
And Moshe was angry against the officers of the army, the officers of the thousands and the officers of the hundreds, who came from the army of the battle.
And Moshe said to them: Have you kept alive all the females?
Behold, they were for the children of Yisroel, by the word of Bilam, to trespass a trespass against Havayah in the matter of Peor, and the plague was in the congregation of Havayah.
And now, kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with a male.
And all the little ones among the women, who have not known lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves.
And you, encamp outside the camp seven days; all who killed a soul, and all who touched a corpse, you shall purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
And every garment, and every skin vessel, and all goats'-hair work, and every wooden vessel, you shall purify.
And Elazar the priest said to the men of the army who came to the battle: This is the statute of the law that Havayah commanded Moshe.
Only the gold, and the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead.

Every thing that comes through fire, you shall pass through fire, and it shall be pure; only, with the sprinkling water it shall be purified; and all that does not come through fire, you shall pass through water.
And you shall wash your garments on the seventh day, and be pure, and afterwards you shall come to the camp.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Take the sum of the plunder of the captives, of man and of animal, you and Elazar the priest and the heads of the fathers of the congregation.
And you shall divide the plunder in half, between those who took part in the war, who went out to the army, and all the congregation.
And you shall set apart a levy to Havayah, from the men of war who went out to the army, one soul from five hundred, from the persons, and from the cattle, and from the donkeys, and from the flocks.
From their half you shall take, and give to Elazar the priest as a gift to Havayah.

And from the half of the children of Yisroel, you shall take one drawn from fifty, from the persons, from the cattle, from the donkeys, from the flocks, from all the animals, and give them to the Leviim, guardians of the charge of the Tabernacle of Havayah.
And Moshe and Elazar the priest did as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And the plunder, the rest of the spoil that the men of the army plundered, was: sheep, six hundred thousand and seventy-five thousand.
And cattle, seventy-two thousand.
And donkeys, sixty-one thousand.
And persons, of the women who had not known lying with a male, thirty-two thousand souls.
And the half, the portion of those who went out to the army, was: the number of the sheep, three hundred and thirty-seven thousand and five hundred.
And the levy to Havayah, from the sheep, was six hundred and seventy-five.
And the cattle, thirty-six thousand, and their levy to Havayah, seventy-two.
And the donkeys, thirty thousand and five hundred, and their levy to Havayah, sixty-one.
And persons, sixteen thousand, and their levy to Havayah, thirty-two souls.
And Moshe gave the levy, the gift of Havayah, to Elazar the priest, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And from the half of the children of Yisroel, that Moshe divided from the men who campaigned.
And the half of the congregation was: from the sheep, three hundred and thirty-seven thousand and five hundred.
And cattle, thirty-six thousand.
And donkeys, thirty thousand and five hundred.
And persons, sixteen thousand.

And Moshe took from the half of the children of Yisroel the one drawn from fifty, from the persons and from the animals, and gave them to the Leviim, guardians of the charge of the Tabernacle of Havayah, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And the officers over the thousands of the army, the officers of the thousands and the officers of the hundreds, approached Moshe.
And they said to Moshe: Your servants took the sum of the men of war who are in our hand, and not one man is missing from us.
And we have brought the offering of Havayah, what a man found, a gold vessel, an armlet, and a bracelet, a ring, an earring, and a girdle, to atone for our souls before Havayah.
And Moshe and Elazar the priest took the gold from them, all wrought vessels.
And all the gold of the gift that they lifted to Havayah was sixteen thousand and seven hundred and fifty shekels, from the officers of the thousands and from the officers of the hundreds.
The men of the army plundered, each man for himself.

And Moshe and Elazar the priest took the gold from the officers of the thousands and from the officers of the hundreds, and brought it to the Tent of Meeting, a remembrance for the children of Yisroel before Havayah.
And the children of Reuven and the children of Gad had much livestock, very much; and they saw the land of Yazer and the land of Gilad, and behold, the place was a place of livestock.
And the children of Gad and the children of Reuven came, and said to Moshe and to Elazar the priest and to the princes of the congregation, saying:
Ataros, and Divon, and Yazer, and Nimrah, and Cheshbon, and Elaleh, and Sevam, and Nevo, and Beon.
The land that Havayah struck before the congregation of Yisroel, it is a land of livestock, and your servants have livestock.
And they said: If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants for a possession; do not take us across the Yarden.
And Moshe said to the children of Gad and to the children of Reuven: Shall your brothers come to war, and you sit here?
And why do you break the heart of the children of Yisroel, keeping them from crossing to the land that Havayah gave them?
So your fathers did, when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to see the land.
And they went up until the valley of Eshkol, and saw the land, and broke the heart of the children of Yisroel, not to come to the land that Havayah gave them.
And the anger of Havayah burned on that day, and He swore, saying:
The men who came up from Mitzrayim, from twenty years old and above, shall not see the land that I swore to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, for they did not follow Me fully.
Except Kalev son of Yefuneh the Kenizite, and Yehoshua son of Nun, for they followed Havayah fully.
And the anger of Havayah burned against Yisroel, and He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the end of all the generation that did evil in the eyes of Havayah.
And behold, you have risen in place of your fathers, a breed of sinful men, to add still to the burning anger of Havayah against Yisroel.
For if you turn away from following Him, He will continue to leave them in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people.
And they approached him, and said: We will build sheepfolds for our livestock here, and cities for our little ones.

And we will go swiftly, armed, before the children of Yisroel, until we have brought them to their place, and our little ones shall dwell in the fortified cities, because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until the children of Yisroel have taken, each man, his inheritance.
For we will not inherit with them across the Yarden and beyond, for our inheritance has come to us, across the Yarden, eastward.
And Moshe said to them: If you do this thing, if you go armed before Havayah to war.
And every armed man among you shall cross the Yarden before Havayah, until He drives out His enemies from before Him.
And the land is conquered before Havayah, and afterwards you shall return, and be clear before Havayah and before Yisroel, and this land shall be yours for a possession before Havayah.
And if you do not do so, behold, you have sinned to Havayah, and know your sin that it will find you.
Build for yourselves cities for your little ones, and folds for your flocks, and what comes out of your mouth, you shall do.
And the children of Gad and the children of Reuven said to Moshe, saying: Your servants shall do as my master commands.
Our little ones, our wives, our livestock, and all our animals, shall be there, in the cities of Gilad.
And your servants shall cross, every man armed for war, before Havayah to war, as my master speaks.
And Moshe commanded concerning them Elazar the priest, and Yehoshua son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yisroel.

And Moshe said to them: If the children of Gad and the children of Reuven cross with you the Yarden, every man armed for war before Havayah, and the land is conquered before you, and you shall give them the land of Gilad for a possession.
And if they do not cross armed with you, they shall take a portion among you in the land of Kena'an.
And the children of Gad and the children of Reuven answered, saying: What Havayah spoke to your servants, so we will do.
We will cross armed before Havayah to the land of Kena'an, and the possession of our inheritance shall be with us, across the Yarden.

And Moshe gave to them, to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuven, and to half the tribe of Menasheh son of Yosef, the kingdom of Sichon, king of the Emorim, and the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan, the land, with its cities, in the borders, the cities of the land around.
And the children of Gad built Divon, and Ataros, and Aroer.
Atros Shofan, and Yazer, and Yogbehah.
Beis Nimrah, and Beis Charan, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.
And the children of Reuven built Cheshbon, and Elaleh, and Kiryasayim.
And Nevo, and Baal Meon, whose names were changed, and Sivmah; and they called names to the cities that they built.
And the children of Machir son of Menasheh went to Gilad, and captured it, and dispossessed the Emorim who were in it.
And Moshe gave Gilad to Machir son of Menasheh, and he dwelt in it.
And Yair son of Menasheh went, and captured their villages, and called them Chavos Yair.
And Novach went, and captured Kenas and its towns, and called it Novach, after his name.
These are the journeys of the children of Yisroel, who came out of the land of Mitzrayim by their hosts, by the hand of Moshe and Aharon.
And Moshe wrote their goings out for their journeys by the word of Havayah; and these are their journeys for their goings out.

And they journeyed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Pesach, the children of Yisroel went out with a high hand, before the eyes of all Mitzrayim.
And the Mitzrim were burying those whom Havayah had smitten among them, all their firstborn; and upon their gods Havayah executed judgments.
And they journeyed from Rameses, and encamped in Sukkos.
And they journeyed from Sukkos, and encamped in Esam.
And they journeyed from Esam, and turned back to Pi HaChiros, which is before Baal Tzefon, and they encamped before Migdol.
And they journeyed from before HaChiros, and crossed through the midst of the sea to the wilderness, and they went a journey of three days in the wilderness of Esam, and encamped in Marah.
And they journeyed from Marah, and came to Eilim; and in Eilim were twelve springs of water and seventy date palms, and they encamped there.
And they journeyed from Eilim, and encamped by the Yam Suf.
And they journeyed from the Yam Suf, and encamped in the wilderness of Sin.
And they journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, and encamped in Dofkah.
And they journeyed from Dofkah, and encamped in Alush.
And they journeyed from Alush, and encamped in Refidim; and there was no water there for the people to drink.
And they journeyed from Refidim, and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.
And they journeyed from the wilderness of Sinai, and encamped in Kivros HaTa'avah.
And they journeyed from Kivros HaTa'avah, and encamped in Chatzeros.
And they journeyed from Chatzeros, and encamped in Rismah.
And they journeyed from Rismah, and encamped in Rimon Peretz.
And they journeyed from Rimon Peretz, and encamped in Livnah.
And they journeyed from Livnah, and encamped in Rissah.
And they journeyed from Rissah, and encamped in Kehelasah.
And they journeyed from Kehelasah, and encamped at Mount Shefer.
And they journeyed from Mount Shefer, and encamped in Charadah.
And they journeyed from Charadah, and encamped in Makhelos.
And they journeyed from Makhelos, and encamped in Tachas.
And they journeyed from Tachas, and encamped in Terach.
And they journeyed from Terach, and encamped in Miskah.
And they journeyed from Miskah, and encamped in Chashmonah.
And they journeyed from Chashmonah, and encamped in Moserot.
And they journeyed from Moserot, and encamped in Bnei Yaakan.
And they journeyed from Bnei Yaakan, and encamped at Chor HaGidgad.
And they journeyed from Chor HaGidgad, and encamped in Yotvasah.
And they journeyed from Yotvasah, and encamped in Avronah.
And they journeyed from Avronah, and encamped in Etzyon Gever.
And they journeyed from Etzyon Gever, and encamped in the wilderness of Tzin, that is Kadesh.
And they journeyed from Kadesh, and encamped at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom.

And Aharon the priest went up Mount Hor by the word of Havayah, and died there, in the fortieth year of the going out of the children of Yisroel from the land of Mitzrayim, in the fifth month, on the first of the month.
And Aharon was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
And the Kena'ani, king of Arad, who dwells in the south, in the land of Kena'an, heard that the children of Yisroel were coming.
And they journeyed from Mount Hor, and encamped in Tzalmonah.
And they journeyed from Tzalmonah, and encamped in Punon.
And they journeyed from Punon, and encamped in Ovos.
And they journeyed from Ovos, and encamped in Iyei HaAvarim, at the border of Moav.
And they journeyed from Iyim, and encamped in Divon Gad.
And they journeyed from Divon Gad, and encamped in Almon Divlasayim.
And they journeyed from Almon Divlasayim, and encamped in the mountains of Avarim, before Nevo.
And they journeyed from the mountains of Avarim, and encamped in the plains of Moav.
And they encamped by the Yarden, from Beis HaYeshimos until Avel HaShitim, in the plains of Moav.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe in the plains of Moav by the Yarden of Yericho, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, and say to them: When you cross the Yarden to the land of Kena'an,

you shall dispossess all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their figured stones, and all their molten images you shall destroy, and all their high places you shall demolish.
And you shall take possession of the land, and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.

And you shall divide the land by lot according to your families: to the many you shall increase his inheritance, and to the few you shall decrease his inheritance; wherever the lot falls for him, it shall be his; according to the tribes of your fathers you shall divide.

But if you do not dispossess the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those whom you leave of them shall be as thorns in your eyes, and as sharp stakes in your sides, and they shall harass you in the land in which you dwell.
And it shall be, as I thought to do to them, so I will do to you.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Command the children of Yisroel, and say to them: When you come to the land of Kena'an, this is the land that shall fall to you for an inheritance, the land of Kena'an by its borders.
And your south side shall be from the wilderness of Tzin alongside Edom, and your south border shall be from the edge of the Salt Sea eastward.
And your border shall turn south of Maaleh Akravim, and pass toward Tzin, and its going out shall be south of Kadesh Barnea, and it shall go out to Chatzar Adar, and pass toward Atzmon.
And the border shall turn from Atzmon toward the Brook of Mitzrayim, and its going out shall be at the Sea.
And the west border shall be for you the Great Sea and its coast; this shall be the west border for you.
And this shall be the north border for you: from the Great Sea you shall mark for yourselves to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you shall mark to the entrance of Chamas, and the going out of the border shall be toward Tzedad.
And the border shall go out to Zifron, and its going out shall be Chatzar Einan; this shall be your north border.
And you shall mark for yourselves for the east border, from Chatzar Einan to Shefam.
And the border shall go down from Shefam to Rivlah, east of Ayin, and the border shall go down and strike the side of the Sea of Kineret eastward.
And the border shall go down to the Yarden, and its going out shall be at the Salt Sea; this shall be your land by its borders all around.
And Moshe commanded the children of Yisroel, saying: This is the land that you shall divide by lot, which Havayah commanded to give to the nine tribes and to the half tribe.

For the tribe of the children of Reuven by their fathers' houses, and the tribe of the children of Gad by their fathers' houses, have taken their inheritance, and half the tribe of Menasheh has taken its inheritance.
The two tribes and the half tribe have taken their inheritance across the Yarden of Yericho eastward.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
These are the names of the men who shall divide the land for you: Elazar the priest, and Yehoshua son of Nun.
And one prince from each tribe you shall take to divide the land.
And these are the names of the men: for the tribe of Yehudah, Kalev son of Yefuneh.
For the tribe of the children of Shimon, Shmuel son of Amihud.
For the tribe of Binyamin, Elidad son of Kislon.
For the tribe of the children of Dan, a prince, Buki son of Yogli.
For the children of Yosef: for the tribe of the children of Menasheh, a prince, Chaniel son of Efod.
For the tribe of the children of Efrayim, a prince, Kemuel son of Shiftan.
For the tribe of the children of Zevulun, a prince, Elitzafan son of Parnach.
For the tribe of the children of Yissachar, a prince, Paltiel son of Azan.
For the tribe of the children of Asher, a prince, Achihud son of Shelomi.
For the tribe of the children of Naftali, a prince, Pedahel son of Amihud.
These are those whom Havayah commanded to divide the inheritance to the children of Yisroel in the land of Kena'an.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe in the plains of Moav by the Yarden of Yericho, saying:

Command the children of Yisroel, and they shall give to the Leviim, from the inheritance of their possession, cities to dwell in, and open land for the cities around them you shall give to the Leviim.
And the cities shall be for them to dwell in, and their open land shall be for their animals, and for their property, and for all their needs.
And the open land of the cities that you shall give to the Leviim, from the wall of the city and outward, one thousand cubits all around.

And you shall measure outside the city, on the east side two thousand cubits, and on the south side two thousand cubits, and on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits, and the city in the middle; this shall be for them the open land of the cities.
And the cities that you shall give to the Leviim, the six cities of refuge that you shall give for the manslayer to flee there; and besides them you shall give forty-two cities.
All the cities that you shall give to the Leviim are forty-eight cities, they and their open land.

And the cities that you shall give from the possession of the children of Yisroel, from the many you shall take many, and from the few you shall take few; each according to his inheritance that he inherits shall give from his cities to the Leviim.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, and say to them: When you cross the Yarden to the land of Kena'an,
you shall designate cities for yourselves; cities of refuge they shall be for you, and the manslayer who strikes a person unwittingly shall flee there.
And the cities shall be for you for refuge from the blood redeemer, and the manslayer shall not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
And the cities that you shall give, six cities of refuge shall be for you.
Three cities you shall give across the Yarden, and three cities you shall give in the land of Kena'an; cities of refuge they shall be.
For the children of Yisroel, and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them, these six cities shall be for refuge, for anyone who strikes a person unwittingly to flee there.
And if he struck him with an iron instrument, and he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
And if he struck him with a stone in the hand, by which one may die, and he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
Or if he struck him with a wooden instrument in the hand, by which one may die, and he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
The redeemer of blood shall put the murderer to death; when he meets him, he shall put him to death.
And if he pushed him out of hatred, or cast upon him by lying in wait, and he died;
or he struck him with his hand in enmity, and he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death; the blood redeemer shall put the murderer to death when he meets him.
But if he pushed him suddenly without enmity, or cast upon him any instrument without lying in wait,
or any stone by which one may die, without seeing him, and he dropped it upon him, and he died, and he was not his enemy, nor did he seek his harm,
then the congregation shall judge between the striker and the blood redeemer, according to these judgments.

And the congregation shall deliver the manslayer from the hand of the blood redeemer, and the congregation shall return him to the city of his refuge, where he fled, and he shall dwell in it until the death of the High Priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the manslayer shall go out from the border of the city of his refuge, to which he fled,
and the blood redeemer finds him outside the border of the city of his refuge, and the blood redeemer kills the manslayer, he has no bloodguilt.
For he shall dwell in the city of his refuge until the death of the High Priest; and after the death of the High Priest, the manslayer shall return to the land of his possession.
And these shall be for you a statute of judgment for your generations, in all your dwellings.
Anyone who strikes a person, by the mouth of witnesses the murderer shall be put to death; but one witness shall not testify against a person to die.
And you shall not take ransom for the life of a murderer, who is guilty to die; for he shall surely be put to death.
And you shall not take ransom for one who fled to the city of his refuge, to return to dwell in the land, until the death of the High Priest.
And you shall not pollute the land in which you are, for blood pollutes the land; and the land shall not be atoned for the blood that is shed in it, except by the blood of him who shed it.
And you shall not defile the land in which you dwell, in which I dwell among you; for I am Havayah, who dwells among the children of Yisroel.

And the heads of the fathers of the family of the children of Gilad son of Machir son of Menasheh, from the families of the children of Yosef, approached, and they spoke before Moshe and before the princes, the heads of the fathers of the children of Yisroel.

And they said: Havayah commanded my master to give the land for an inheritance by lot to the children of Yisroel, and my master was commanded by Havayah to give the inheritance of Tzelofchad our brother to his daughters.

And should they become wives to one of the sons of the tribes of the children of Yisroel, their inheritance shall be deducted from the inheritance of our fathers, and it shall be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they shall belong, and from the lot of our inheritance it shall be deducted.

And when the Jubilee comes for the children of Yisroel, their inheritance shall be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they shall belong, and from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers their inheritance shall be deducted.
And Moshe commanded the children of Yisroel by the word of Havayah, saying: The tribe of the children of Yosef speaks rightly.

This is the word that Havayah commanded for the daughters of Tzelofchad, saying: To the one who is good in their eyes they shall become wives; only, to the family of the tribe of their father shall they become wives.
And no inheritance of the children of Yisroel shall pass from tribe to tribe, for each of the children of Yisroel shall cling to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

And every daughter who inherits an inheritance from the tribes of the children of Yisroel shall become a wife to one from the family of the tribe of her father, so that the children of Yisroel shall inherit, each man the inheritance of his fathers.
And no inheritance shall pass from tribe to another tribe, for the tribes of the children of Yisroel shall cling, each man to his inheritance.
As Havayah commanded Moshe, so the daughters of Tzelofchad did.
And Machlah, Tirtzah, Choglah, Milkah, and Noa, daughters of Tzelofchad, became wives to the sons of their uncles.
They became wives from the families of the children of Menasheh son of Yosef, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of the family of their father.
These are the commandments and the ordinances that Havayah commanded by the hand of Moshe to the children of Yisroel, in the plains of Moav, by the Yarden of Yericho.
